text.p: Algeria's leadership and about 1,000 politicians started a crucial conference at 10.07 a.m. (0907 GMT) on Saturday to try to end nearly five years of violence in which about 50,000 people have been killed.
Algerian state-run television, in a live broadcast, showed President Liamine Zeroual and army chief of staff Mohamed Lamari, standing with former leaders for the National Anthem and opening.

The authorities have blamed the violence on Moslem fundamentalists and are seeking a consensus for political reform. The disputed conference is boycotted by the main secular opposition. Islamists have been barred from attending.
